OOS_protocol.data_window: to be fixed in the registration before any data is read
OOS_protocol.train_test_boundary: later days of the recorded book/trade tape

capacity_model.note: tiny; edge, not size, is the question

counterparty: liquidity takers crossing the spread; informed flow is the loss side
economic_mechanism: Counterparty: impatient takers who pay the spread; informed takers who win against stale quotes are the adverse-selection cost and usually exceed the spread for a slow, small participant. Persists for fast, well-queued makers; disappears for anyone slower than the informed flow, which describes this repo's latency (REST, no co-location).
eligibility_rules: spread wider than 2 * (maker fee + expected adverse selection)
entry: post both sides at registered offsets
execution_model: passive limit orders, queue position modelled from real depth
exit: inventory limit or time stop, cross to flatten
hypothesis: A market maker quoting both sides captures the bid-ask spread net of adverse selection and inventory cost.
prospective_protocol: forward shadow quoting with measured fills before any order
rejection_conditions: no trade tape: fills cannot be simulated honestly, the test is refused
realised spread minus adverse selection at the modelled horizon not positive
fill rate depends on optimistic queue assumptions
net edge after measured maker fee not positive

required_data.gap: only periodic snapshots/quotes; no tick trade tape
required_data.name: L2 book plus trade-by-trade history with exchange timestamps
own order latency and queue position measurements
maker fee/rebate schedule as measured on the account

risk_model: adverse selection; inventory accumulation in a trend; stale quotes on a connection fault
status_note: SPECIFICATION ONLY. Nothing has been tested; this is not a winner. bias_declarations state what the protocol must rule out before any evidence counts, not that it has been ruled out.
